newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron gunman seen as fierce ideologue and loner.
newsitem.headline: Hebron gunman seen as fierce ideologue and loner.

text.p: Noam Friedman, the off-duty Israeli soldier who sprayed automatic rifle fire at Arab shoppers in a Hebron market on Wednesday, was a fierce ideologue described as a loner with a record of mental health problems.

Wrestled to the ground and arrested after wounding seven Palestinaians, two critically, Friedman, 22, proudly told reporters a few hours later that his aim was prevent Israel from turning the West Bank town over to Palestinian self-rule.

"Abraham bought the Cave of the Patriarchs for 400 shekels of silver, Friedman declared, waving his fist in the air and citing the biblical story by which Jews trace their claim to Hebron back 4,000 years.
"No one will return it," he said.
The Cave, where 29 Moslems were massacred by settler Baruch Goldstein three years ago, is holy both to Jews and Moslems.
Israel and the PLO are on the verge of sealing a deal which Israel would turn over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO self-rule. But Friedman set out to stop the deal with his M-16 rifle .

"Hebron is ours now and forever," he told Israel television with a defiance reminiscent of Yigal Amir, another religious Jew who killed prime minister Yitzhak Rabin keep him from giving West Bank lands to the Palestinians.
Friedman was the son of a high school teacher and an employee of Israel's electric company from a quiet neighbourhood of Maaleh Adumim settlement near Jerusalem.
"This was a regular family," Maaleh Adumim Mayor Benny Kashriel told Israel television. The television said Friedman's grandmother, Esther Reiss, was a survivor of the Nazi Holocaust.

One elderly neighbour was stunned to hear of the boy next door's shooting spree. "The whole family, especially Noam, was always ready to help me. I just don't believe it," Monette Zamgriss told the television.

Friedman's mother Riva said her son's behavior took her by surprise. "We educated our children and will continue to educate them for tolerance, respect of human honour and the holiness of human life, every human," she told reporters.
But Friedman expressed no remorse for opening fire on shoppers. "They are not innocent, they hate Israel," he said.
Israel's Itim domestic news agency quoted Friedman's neighbours, acquaintances, and fellow soldiers as saying he was extremely introverted and spoke little. One neighbour described him as a "weirdo".
Israeli media said Friedman had a history of mental health problems. Itim said his recruitment into the army had been delayed by several months because of psychological problems.

Israel radio said teachers at a Jerusalem religious school had recently pressed Freidman to leave after he had "behaved strangely", saying that God had appeared to him and that he had a "mission" to complete.
Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Itim Friedman had twice been turned to mental health officers during his six months of army service.

An Israeli army spokesman said the army had ordered an investigation into Friedman's mental and medical profile and to determine how and why he was issued a weapon. Israel television said Friedman served as an army janitor.
But the gunman maintained his act was good for Israel and insisted his mental health was sound. Asked by Israel television whether he thought he was normal, Friedman replied: "absolutely normal".
